page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96 is a general purpose compute instance powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processors running at a base clock frequency of 2.3 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled across two threads per core. Memory allocation totals 360.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 3.75 GB per vCPU. The instance features dedicated CPU allocation and substantial cache resources, incorporating 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. There are zero dedicated GPUs bundled with this instance type, and it does not include complimentary local storage or free public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute execution and high data throughput. Multi-threaded evaluations highlight top-tier capabilities, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,415.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 83,403.58. Extended instruction set support is comprehensive, featuring AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) and AVX-512 extensions that yield 101,100.9 points on the PassMark extended instructions test and 87,093.55 points on encryption workloads. Memory throughput is also pronounced, reaching 288.83 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations alongside 123.85 GB/sec in write operations. In contrast, single-core metrics fall largely within standard ranges, such as a stress-ng single-core score of 2,103.98.

The hardware configuration achieves notable density for heavy enterprise processing without the operational overhead of specialized hardware accelerators. While single-thread performance is modest, the balanced compute-to-memory ratio and matrix processing acceleration allow strong CPU-based LLM prompt processing, achieving 4,350.33 tokens/sec on 135M parameter models and 289.79 tokens/sec on 7B models. Primary tradeoffs include the lack of local NVMe disks, requiring external network block storage for persistence.

This server type is engineered for large-scale enterprise services, multi-threaded compiling, web serving infrastructures, high-throughput caching, and distributed data analytics. Measured throughput of 126.92 GB/sec in static web serving and 106.4 million operations per second in Redis SET operations reflect high compatibility with memory-intensive backend applications and in-memory caches.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96 is a general purpose x86_64 server driven by Intel Xeon 8581C processors delivering 96 dedicated vCPUs (48 physical cores) at 2.3 GHz and 360.0 GB of RAM. The instance features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions. It does not include local storage or attached GPUs. Benchmark results place its multi-core capabilities in upper tiers, highlighted by a multi-core Geekbench score of 21,415.0, static web serving throughput of 126.92 GB/sec, and 106.4 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware tradeoffs include reliance on external persistent storage and standard-tier single-core performance. The system is well structured for large-scale multi-threaded web services, CPU-based machine learning inference, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and database caching engines.
